entry.title: Signed secrets and safer sign-in
entry.content:
A security release. Update the CLI, then have an editor run noenv secret sign in each environment.

Added

  • noenv secret sign re-saves secrets that an older noenv or the dashboard wrote, after you check their names.
  • noenv rotate makes a new environment key, re-encrypts every secret, and shares the key with the current key holders.
  • noenv trust accepts a new environment key after an admin rotated it.
  • noenv status and noenv grant show key fingerprints, so you can check a key with its owner.

Changed

  • Each secret version is signed with the environment key. The CLI skips a value without a valid signature, so a server or a stolen session token cannot forge one. After you update, an editor runs noenv secret sign once in each environment.
  • The CLI checks that the server's environment key matches the key it unwraps, and pins it on first use.
  • Terminal sign-in shows your device in the dashboard. You type the code and confirm with your passkey.
  • Delete mode no longer uploads .env values in the background. A file with new names waits for noenv migrate.
  • Names that change how code runs, such as PATH, PROMPT_COMMAND, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_* and GIT_*, are reserved. The CLI never exports them.

entry.title: The deployment in .noenv picks the account
entry.content:
Each repository's .noenv file names its deployment, and every teammate gets the same account name from the deployment.

Added

  • noenv account add URL asks the deployment for its team name and saves the account under it. Admins set the name with TEAM_NAME at deploy time. noenv account add URL NAME still sets your own name.

Changed

  • noenv init saves the deployment URL in .noenv. With more than one account, it asks which one to use. Agents pass noenv init --account NAME.
  • The shell hook, noenv exec, and all other commands use the local account whose URL matches .noenv, whatever its name. Teammates can name the account differently.
  • If no local account has that URL, noenv prints the command to add it. It never connects to a URL from .noenv on its own.

Removed

  • Repository prefixes. Run noenv init in each repository to save its deployment.

entry.title: The shell signs you in on its own again
entry.content:
Opening a terminal in a repository starts and finishes the sign-in, instead of asking you to run noenv auth.

Fixed

  • The background sign-in keeps waiting through network errors, server errors, and rate limits. Before, a Wi-Fi drop or a laptop waking from sleep stopped it.
  • When a sign-in is pending but the process that waits for it has stopped, the shell starts a new one.
  • After a sign-in fails or its code expires, entering the repository again starts a new sign-in.

entry.title: Agents, Wrangler push, and named accounts
entry.content:
Coding agents and CI get their secrets with one command, secrets push to Cloudflare Workers, and one CLI works with several teams.

Added

  • noenv exec -- CMD runs a command with the secrets of the repository in the current directory. It is for coding agents, scripts, and CI, where the cd hook does not run.
  • noenv wrangler [KEY…] pushes secrets to your Worker with wrangler secret bulk. Without keys, it shows a list to pick from.
  • A [wrangler] section in .noenv pushes the listed keys after each secret set and secret rollback.
  • noenv secret set reads a piped value, so agents can save a secret without a prompt.
  • Admins can cancel a pending invite from Overview or Team. The invite link stops working at once.
  • noenv account add NAME URL [PREFIX…] saves a deployment as a named account. Repositories under a prefix such as github.com/acme use it.
  • noenv account list, account default, and account remove.
  • noenv auth NAME signs in to one account.
  • When you cd from a repository of one account to a repository of another, noenv unloads the first set of secrets and loads the second.

Changed

  • A cd decrypts the last bundle on your machine and makes no network request. A background refresh loads newer values when they arrive.
  • noenv init creates a .noenv file. Commit it, so access problems show as messages instead of silence.

entry.title: CLI on npm, email invites, and a new name
entry.content:
The product is now noenv, the CLI installs from npm, and invites can go out by email.

Added

  • The CLI is on npm as @thisisamank/noenv-cli. The command stays noenv.
  • Invites and the first admin's setup link can go out by email through Cloudflare Email Sending. Set EMAIL_FROM to turn it on.
  • This website, with the 40-second tour.

Changed

  • nenv is now noenv. The old website address redirects to the new one.
  • The Deploy button no longer asks for an email sender. Keep EMAIL_FROM as none to send invite links yourself.
  • Polished the dashboard and the page the Worker serves.

entry.title: First release
entry.content:
Encrypted environment variables that load when you cd into a repository, on your own Cloudflare account.

Added

  • Secrets load when you cd into a git repository and unload when you leave. zsh and bash.
  • Values are encrypted on your machine. The Worker stores only ciphertext.
  • Every change is a new version, with history and rollback.
  • Sign-in with passkeys. Roles: reader, editor, and admin.
  • noenv migrate moves .env files in and verifies every value.
  • .env policies (warn, block, migrate, delete), minimum CLI version, and session expiry.
  • The dashboard: projects, secrets, team, policies, and devices.
  • One-click Deploy to Cloudflare.

Fixed

  • The Deploy button build failed on an old package name in the lock file.
